identity.title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents

problem.claim: Evaluate general-purpose LLM agents across diverse scenarios, including partially observable environments and multi-round interactions, within a unified framework.

gap.claim: Existing evaluation frameworks mainly report final success rates, offering limited process insight and an insufficiently deep account of agent abilities.

contributions.claim: Introduces AgentBoard, a comprehensive benchmark with an accompanying open-source framework for analytical evaluation of LLM agents.
Provides a fine-grained progress-rate metric for incremental advancement and an evaluation toolkit supporting multifaceted analysis through interactive visualization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize AgentBoard as a pioneering comprehensive benchmark and open-source analytical evaluation framework tailored to LLM agents.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the progress-rate metric captures incremental advancements during agent evaluation.
The authors report that interactive visualization enables multifaceted assessment and helps expose agent capabilities and limitations.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM-agent evaluation is presented as important for understanding capabilities and supporting practical integration.
The paper identifies difficulties in unified benchmarking across diverse, partially observable, multi-round settings.
It argues that final-success-rate evaluation provides little insight into the interaction process or underlying abilities.
AgentBoard combines a comprehensive benchmark, an open-source toolkit, a progress-rate metric, and interactive visualization for analytical evaluation.
The authors say this supports interpretation of agent performance and helps demystify agent behavior.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a process-sensitive progress metric with interactive visualization to address the limited insight of final success rates.

lessons.interpretation: Intermediate measurements can make multi-turn agent behavior more interpretable than endpoint scores alone.
lessons.application: For a multi-step system, report trajectory-level progress alongside final outcomes and visualize where advancement stalls.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when intermediate states are unavailable, poorly defined, or not meaningfully comparable across tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not report benchmark tasks, dataset scale, baselines, numerical results, or details of how progress rate is computed.
The abstract does not establish that AgentBoard improves agent performance, nor does it independently verify the authors' claims of pioneering status or significance.
